source_name: Banka Slovenije – Pravni okvir (legal framework database, filterable)
why_relevant: Single densest first-party register of the legal acts Banka Slovenije applies and issues: filterable by podrocje (monetary policy, financial stability, banking supervision, payment systems, statistics), kategorija/podkategorija and vrsta (national legislation, EU regulation, directive, ECB acts, EBA guidelines, internal acts). Observed ~1,208 entries with SL/EN toggles and direct PDF links. This is the canonical entry point for tracking which sklepi/uredbe are in force for SI banks and PSPs.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Nadzor bančnega sistema (banking supervision hub)
why_relevant: Top-level supervision section from which all supervisory sub-streams branch (regulativni okvir, nadzorniške prakse, licenciranje, razkritja, AML, restrictive measures, consumer credit). Best single node to snowball supervisory publications and to detect new sub-sections appearing.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Regulativni okvir (prudential rulebook explainer, CRD/CRR, ESG, EMIR/SFTR, covered bonds)
why_relevant: BS's own framing of which EU/regulatory blocks bind Slovenian banks (CRD/CRR, sustainable finance/ESG, EMIR & SFTR, covered bonds) and where implementation questions go. Contains an official Q&A/submission form for regulatory interpretation — a signal channel for implementation friction and upcoming clarifications.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Nadzorniške prakse, postopki in ukrepi (SREP, SEP, stress tests, letters to banks)
why_relevant: Describes the supervisory cycle that generates deadlines: three-year strategic supervisory priorities, annual Supervisory Examination Programme (SEP) per bank, annual SREP producing P2R/P2G, and annual stress tests (archived 2011–2025). Also hosts the governor's annual 'letters to banks' — a high-signal statement of supervisory expectations for the coming year.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Nadzorniška razkritja in seznami (supervisory disclosures, CRD Art.143)
why_relevant: Mandatory CRD supervisory disclosure: how SI transposed CRD/CRR, national options and discretions, aggregate supervisory data, and lists. This is where the mapping between EU rule and Slovenian national implementation (including transposition dates) is documented in one place.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Nadzor nebančnih ponudnikov plačilnih storitev in infrastruktur finančnega trga
why_relevant: The payments-side supervisory/oversight node: licensing of payment institutions and e-money issuers under ZPlaSSIED, registers of licensed and exempt providers, AISP register, oversight of the four SI payment systems (incl. TARGET-Slovenija) and the KDD securities settlement system, plus FX bureau (menjalci) supervision. Directly generates authorisation decisions, reporting obligations and deadlines for payment-sector actors.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Plačilni sistemi (payments hub incl. digital euro, SEPA, National Payments Council)
why_relevant: Umbrella for the payments workstream: payment instruments, payment/e-money services, accounts, SEPA, Nacionalni svet za plačila (NSP), payment infrastructure, market-infrastructure advisory groups, digital euro, oversight, FAQ. Useful for spotting forthcoming payments-regulatory change (instant payments, digital euro, PSD3/PSR readiness) before formal acts appear.

source_name: Nacionalni svet za plačila (National Payments Council) – minutes and papers hosted by Banka Slovenije
why_relevant: NSP session minutes (e.g. document ref NSP/2025/018, 'Zapisnik 36. seje Nacionalnega sveta za plačila') are published as PDFs and record forthcoming payment-market changes, migration timetables and industry positions ahead of formal regulation — an early-warning channel for payments deadlines in Slovenia.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Poročanje (reporting obligations for reporting entities)
why_relevant: Where reporting obligations and their submission calendars live. Individual report pages (e.g. ITS supervisory reporting, deposit guarantee scheme reporting) carry legal basis, scope and due dates — i.e. recurring compliance deadlines rather than one-off ones.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Tehnična navodila in XML sheme (technical reporting instructions)
why_relevant: Versioned technical instructions and XML schemas per reporting stream (KRD/BST/SN, ITS, PPDFT, SISBIZ/B2B, PORECB, RTPS, SPI2/SPI3, VIRI-VEP and others). Schema version bumps with effective dates are a precise, machine-readable leading indicator of impending reporting-rule changes and their compliance dates.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Arhiv navodil (archive of superseded instructions)
why_relevant: Historical archive of withdrawn/superseded BS instructions. Valuable for reconstructing the timeline of a rule (when a navodilo was replaced, and by what) — i.e. retrospective deadline and transition-period reconstruction.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Sporočila za javnost / Mediji (press releases & news)
why_relevant: Announcement layer: new decisions of the Svet Banke Slovenije, macroprudential measure changes, supervisory findings and consultation openings are typically announced here first, often days before the act appears in the official gazette. Section offers an email newsletter subscription ('Prijavite se na novice') — a low-cost push channel. Sub-streams: Sporočila za javnost, Govori in intervjuji, Publikacije, Centralni pogled podcast.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Finančna stabilnost / Makrobonitetni instrumenti
why_relevant: Macroprudential instrument settings (buffer rates, borrower-based measures) are adopted as BS sklepi with explicit application dates and phase-in periods — a dense source of forward-dated compliance deadlines for banks. Also links the Odbor za finančno stabilnost and the macroprudential policy strategic framework.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Katalog informacij javnega značaja (public information catalogue)
why_relevant: Statutorily required catalogue that enumerates the laws governing BS AND the sklepi and other regulations adopted by the Svet Banke Slovenije, plus the routes for freedom-of-information requests. Acts as an authoritative index/pointer to the full corpus of BS general acts, and documents the legal channel for requesting non-published material.

source_name: Uradni list Republike Slovenije – official gazette (BS general acts publication venue)
why_relevant: Banka Slovenije publishes the general acts adopted by its Council in the Official Gazette; the gazette text is the legally binding version and carries the entry-into-force and compliance dates ('uskladiti … v roku'). Includes per-issue tables of contents (celotno-kazalo) enabling systematic issue-by-issue harvesting. NOTE (hypothesis, needs verification): search results indicate issues published after 28 Feb 2026 are made available via PISRS rather than the classic uradni-list flow — the publication pipeline may have changed.

source_name: PISRS – Pravno-informacijski sistem RS (consolidated legal register)
why_relevant: Authoritative consolidated ('neuradno prečiščeno besedilo') texts of Slovenian acts including BS sklepi, with amendment history and stable IDs (e.g. SKLE13896, ZAKO2988). Essential for determining the currently applicable text and the chain of amendments behind a deadline. Search results also indicate PISRS has become the destination for gazette content published after 28 Feb 2026 — raising its priority.

source_name: E-demokracija (eUprava) – Predlogi predpisov (public consultation portal)
why_relevant: The state's formal public-consultation portal where draft laws affecting banking/payments (e.g. Zakon o spremembah in dopolnitvah Zakona o bančništvu, EVA 2024-1611-0034, sent 5.2.2025) are opened for comment with explicit consultation windows. Banka Slovenije itself does not appear to run a standing public-consultation register on bsi.si, so primary-legislation consultation signal for the SI banking framework surfaces here (proposer: Ministrstvo za finance) rather than at the NCB.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Reševanje bank / Jamstvo za vloge (resolution & deposit guarantee)
why_relevant: BS acts as national resolution authority and manages the deposit guarantee scheme; both generate binding acts, MREL-type requirements, contribution deadlines and reporting obligations distinct from prudential supervision.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Preprečevanje pranja denarja in financiranja terorizma (AML/CFT supervision)
why_relevant: AML/CFT is the sub-domain with the densest near-term deadline flow for SI banks and payment institutions (EU AML package / AMLA transition, AMLD 2015/849 → 2024/1640). BS publishes guidance, expectations and the PPDFT reporting stream here.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Finančni omejevalni ukrepi (financial restrictive measures / sanctions)
why_relevant: Sanctions-compliance expectations and notices for supervised entities; changes here typically carry immediate (same-day) implementation obligations, making it a high-tempo deadline source.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Informacije o izrečenih ukrepih (published supervisory measures/sanctions)
why_relevant: Mandatory publication of supervisory measures and penalties imposed on named institutions. Reveals de facto enforcement priorities and which requirements are actually being tested — the strongest indirect evidence of where compliance pressure sits.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Letno poročilo (annual report) and Poročilo o finančni stabilnosti
why_relevant: Annual Report contains a dedicated retrospective account of regulatory and supervisory activity for the year (acts adopted, measures taken, consultations participated in); the Financial Stability Report explains macroprudential decisions and signals forthcoming ones. Publication section also exposes a forward calendar of planned release dates — useful for scheduling collection.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Kazalo vsebine (full site index / sitemap)
why_relevant: Human-curated full sitemap of bsi.si. The cheapest reliable way to enumerate every relevant BS page (including low-traffic ones such as the fintech contact point, technical guidelines, and supervisory disclosure pages) and to detect newly created sections over time.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – English site (bsi.si/en) as parallel-language mirror
why_relevant: BS maintains an English mirror (e.g. /en/media) and many legal-framework entries expose SL/EN document pairs. Useful for terminology alignment and for extraction pipelines that work better in English — but coverage is a subset of the SL site, so SL must remain the collection master. Note: the intuitive English path /en/legislation returned 404, so English URL paths are not a simple translation of the SL slugs.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (Bank Association of Slovenia) – news and positions
why_relevant: The industry body that responds to BS/MF consultations on behalf of banks. Its statements often reveal which draft requirements and deadlines the industry considers burdensome, and sometimes surface consultation drafts or implementation timetables not prominently posted by BS itself. Indirect (interested party) — corroborate against the first-party act.

source_name: ATVP – Agencija za trg vrednostnih papirjev (official website / news)
why_relevant: Slovenian securities market supervisor. Publishes news, decisions (sklepi) on whether ESMA/EBA guidelines apply in Slovenia, and supervisory expectations that bind banks acting as investment firms / providing investment services under MiFID II.

source_name: ATVP – Javni posveti / consultations announcements (ESMA draft documents)
why_relevant: ATVP relays ESMA public consultations to Slovenian market participants, usually with national response deadlines — a primary early-warning signal for upcoming obligations on banks providing investment services.
